newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to halt Zaporizhya alumina output.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to halt Zaporizhya alumina output.

text.p: KIEV, Dec 9 (Reeuter) - Ukraine is to halt output of alumina at its energy-inefficient Zaporizhya smelter, using supplies from the Mykolaiv smelter to produce aluminium at Zaporizhya, Industry Minister Valery Mazur told a news conference on Monday.
"We plan, within the framework of our aluminium sector modernisation programme, to close Zaporizhya's alumina section because it requires too much energy," Mazur said.
"The Zaporizhya plant has been working for many years and needs reconstruction and modernisation."
Mazur said Ukraine planned to bring 200,000 tonnes of alumina annually from the Mykolaiv plant -- Europe's largest -- to Zaporizhya for aluminium production.
Mazur said Zaporizhya had used an Italian credit line to construct modern facilities to produce aluminium foil with the Italian company Fata.
"In a year and a half we will have modern foil production at the Zaporizhya plant," Mazur said.
Ukraine has forecast 1997 alumina production at 1.2 million tonnes and aluminium output at 90,000 tonnes.

It produced 80,900 tonnes of aluminium between January and November this year, down seven percent from the same period last year. January to November alumina production fell four percent to 1.06 million tonnes, compared with the same period last year.

"At some point we plan to create a holding company or concern uniting the two factories, but the question is still open and are far from being decided," Mazur said. "Right now we are working out the financial questions around this."
The bulk of Ukraine's alumina is exported to Russia for smelting. --Irene Marushko, Kiev Newsroom +380 44 229 2264
